2026-12-09.title: Second Wednesday of Annunciation
2026-12-09.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Behold the handmaid of the Lord
2026-12-09.verse: For nothing will be impossible with God.
theo: Paul blesses God who “chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love.” God's plan for each of us began before we were born; our vocation is to say yes to it.

Mary's question, “How can this be?”, is not doubt but a desire to understand. The answer reveals the Holy Spirit's power and gives a sign, Elizabeth's pregnancy, “for nothing will be impossible with God.” Mary then gives herself completely: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord.”
outline: Ask: what seems impossible in your life right now?
God's plan for you is older than the world.
Faith seeks understanding and then trusts.
God's power is greater than our limits.
live: Write down one “impossible” situation and pray over it daily.
Thank God for your state of life and renew your commitment.
2026-12-09.prayer: Father, you chose me in Christ before the foundation of the world. With Mary I give you my yes, for nothing is impossible with you. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Holy Spirit overshadows the gifts as he overshadowed Mary, and the Word becomes present among us. We answer with Mary: let it be done to me.

quick: God chose us in Christ before the world began.
Mary's question seeks understanding, not proof.
2026-12-09.question: What seems impossible to me, and have I given it to God?

family.explain: Mary did not understand everything, but she trusted God and said yes. Nothing is impossible for God.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family facing something that seems impossible.
family.ask: Ask: “Where does God want each of us to say yes this week?”

pm.open: Blessed be God, who chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world. As we gather, give us Mary's trust and Mary's yes. Amen.
share: Paul says God chose me before the foundation of the world (Ephesians 1:4). How does that change the way I see myself?
Mary asked: how can this be? (Luke 1:34). What question do I bring to God today?
Where is God asking for my yes?
pm.resp: Here am I, Lord; let it be done according to your word.
interc: For the Church, that, like Mary, she may always say yes to God.
For those facing impossible situations: illness, debt, broken relationships, that they may trust God.
For young people discerning their vocation, that they may hear God's call.
For couples longing for children, like Elizabeth.
For all of us, that this Christmas God's word may take flesh in our lives.
pm.close: Lord God, you chose us before the world was made and you call us to share your life. With Mary, we say: here am I. Do with us according to your word. Amen.

illus: A young woman from a poor family in Idukki felt called to become a nurse but had no money for the course. Her parish priest helped her find a scholarship. Years later, as head nurse in a large hospital, she said: “I asked God: how can this be? He answered through people.” Nothing is impossible with God.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul opens his letter to the Ephesians with a hymn of blessing: blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing (Ephesians 1:3). Before we ask God for anything, Paul teaches us to bless him.

He continues: he chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love; he destined us for adoption as his children (Ephesians 1:4–5). Before the stars were made, God knew you and chose you. Your life is not an accident.

In the Gospel we return to Nazareth. Mary, hearing that she will conceive the Son of the Most High, asks: how can this be, since I am a virgin? (Luke 1:34). It is a real question. Mary does not pretend to understand everything. Faith is not the absence of questions; it is trust that God has an answer.

The angel answers: the Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; and he adds: nothing will be impossible with God (Luke 1:35–37). Elizabeth, old and childless, is pregnant: a sign that God can do what seems impossible.

Then Mary says the words that changed history: here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word (Luke 1:38). God's eternal plan, chosen before the foundation of the world, became real through the free yes of a young woman.
God has a plan for you too: for your family, your work, your vocation. Sometimes it seems impossible. You may ask, like Mary: how can this be? Ask, but then trust. Nothing is impossible with God.
Today, let us pray Mary's words slowly: here am I, the servant of the Lord. Let us say them about one concrete area of our lives where God is asking for our yes. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary said yes to God. You can say yes to God every day by being kind and obedient!

intro: Theme: “Nothing will be impossible with God.”
Chosen in Christ; Mary's question and consent.

points.h: Chosen before the foundation of the world
sub: Each vocation is part of it.
q: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you.
Mary said to the angel, “How can this be, since I am a virgin?”

points.h: The power of the Most High
sub: God's power accomplishes what nature cannot.
q: Is anything too wonderful for the LORD?
For nothing will be impossible with God.
points.apply: Give God one impossible situation today.

sub: Her yes is free and total.
q: And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
Then Mary said, “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.”
points.apply: Say “Here I am, Lord” at the start of each day.

concl: God's plan is greater than our limits.
Let us answer with Mary: here I am.
